To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and demonstrated a new method for the radiographic imaging of cargo containers that is suitable for the detection of nuclear materials.

the use of dual energies in radioscopic inspection of cargo is feasible and that the dual energy radioscopic inspection of containers is a viable alternative for the inspection of cargo for the presence of contraband.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of using the 6 MeV boundary energy for the radioscopic screening of cargo containers and that this technology facilitates the material identifications by measuring the ratios of signals at nominal and dual boundary energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
development of new technologies for the detection of special objects of interests, which can be used in the inspection of cargo and other objects.
the development of a novel method of cargo screening by using the dual-energy X-ray transmission radiography with the boundary energies of 6 and 8 MeV.
the development of a radioscopic inspection system that is capable to detect the presence and the location of nuclear materials in cargo containers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this technology can be used to inspect cargo containers and to identify the contents.
the radioscopic screening of the contents of cargo containers with the megavoltage dual energy boundary is a very promising technology.
the dual energy radioscopic inspection of cargo is feasible and can be used for detection of objects that are hidden behind the steel shields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radioscopic inspection of cargo with megavoltage energies is feasible.
we can identify the objects of interests with the thickness of 1/3 of the shielding thickness.
the dual energy imaging technique has been successfully developed for the radioscopic inspection of cargo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual-energy radioscopic screening is a viable technique to detect the objects of interest in cargo containers.
the dual energy radioscopic imaging is a powerful tool to detect nuclear materials.
the inspection of cargo container with the megavoltage energy barrier can be done with the use of a single source and detector pair.
